name: cratylism
wording: the corpus's first principle: a name is natural, not conventional. A model's semantic space holds real, stable concepts, so the sign of each core term of the corpus, the agents context's factor names and values, is its optimal sign, discovered by the cold-decode oracle and never coined by an author or an operator. Every other term takes its natural name in its own context, the industry's own word used as the industry understands it, and no consumer's surfaces are held to the oracle. The optimal sign is an ideal approached: where a kept sign falls short of it, the shortfall is recorded as real, never explained away.
reason: Decision 0049 states this as the signify principle, but the corpus's locked first principle already names it cratylism, and one concept keeps one sign, so it is defined under its locked name in the words of its locked statement. Its scope is what separates the oracle's work from naming in every other context: why the workflow keeps assayer by its natural name in context (0042) and capability interface dropped cold names.
